classification.difficultyReason: Translate two rearrangements into perimeter equations and combine them.

content.prompt: Rectangle $A$ has dimensions $x\,\mathrm{cm}\times y\,\mathrm{cm}$. The rectangle may be cut in half vertically and its parts rearranged to give rectangle $B$, which has a perimeter of $30$ cm. Rectangle $A$ may also be cut in half horizontally and its parts rearranged to give rectangle $C$, which has a perimeter of $45$ cm. Find the perimeter of rectangle $A$.

spec.sourceRegion: Top of right column, continuation of question 12
spec.description: A, B and C appear in one paired comparison row. B has a solid horizontal join; C has a dashed vertical join. Decorative source red fill is omitted.
spec.mathematics: A has dimensions x by y; B comprises two x/2 by y pieces stacked; C comprises two x by y/2 pieces side by side.
spec.answerVisibility: Only A carries the supplied dimension labels.

answer.short:
$30\,\mathrm{cm}$

Add the two rearranged perimeter equations to obtain $x+y=15$ cm.
answer.worked:
Rectangle $B$ has dimensions $\frac{x}{2}$ cm by $2y$ cm; rectangle $C$ has dimensions $2x$ cm by $\frac{y}{2}$ cm.
$$\begin{align*}2\left(\frac{x}{2}+2y\right)&=30\\x+4y&=30\\2\left(2x+\frac{y}{2}\right)&=45\\4x+y&=45.\end{align*}$$
Adding the two simplified equations gives
$$\begin{align*}5x+5y&=75\\x+y&=15\\P_A&=2(x+y)\\P_A&=30\,\mathrm{cm}.\end{align*}$$
